newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cruising Brussels bourse heads happily higher.
newsitem.headline: Cruising Brussels bourse heads happily higher.

text.p: Buoyant sentiment, the dollar, low interest rates and a rising New York combined to lift the Brussels bourse to new highs in active business on Friday, and traders said the market retained a good head of steam.
"Our feeling is that as long as interest rates remain low in Europe it will be good for the equities markets," one trader said.
Traders said there was no special reason for the strength of the Brussels market on Friday.
"All European markets are very strong. Today it was the turn of Brussels. There is no specific reason," one said.

The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares ended 1.18 percent higher at a new closing high of 2,309.93 after earlier setting a new intra-day high of 2,313.06 -- comfortably above the 2,300 level some analysts had set as the target for the end of 1997.
A total of 3.7 billion francs of Belgian shares were traded.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere and steel firm Arbed were the darlings of the market, boosted by foreign buyers latching onto the improving prospects of the two firms, traders said.
Arbed was up 5.9 percent to 4,195 francs with 160,000 shares traded.
Union Miniere was up 3.9 percent to 3,200 francs in a volume of more than 105,000 shares.
Traders said Arbed gained on improving steel sector prospects, while Union Miniere benefitted from the strong dollar and zinc prices and solid sentiment.
There is also the prospect of UM getting more involved in copper and cobalt in the Democratic Republic of Congo -- formerly Zaire.
Chief Executive Officer Karel Vinck visited the country last month after the revolution that ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko.
"There is a very positive and growing feeling for Union Miniere. People are starting to think of the good old days when its share price was an indicator of the state of the country," one trader said.

The firm dollar also helped other shares such as retailer Delhaize, up 1.1 percent, shipper CMB, up one percent, and chemical firm Solvay, up 2.5 percent -- although the latter was also helped by a forthcoming 10 for one share split.
Among the cyclicals, cement maker CBR was a strong performer, rising 1.7 percent to 3,360 francs.

Power utility Electrabel, which suffered heavily for the past few days on talk of a possible merger with little brother Tractebel, regained some of its previous poise to rise 0.5 percent to 7,660 francs.

Traders said the recovery was due to some doubts about the merger going ahead and a feeling that if in any case it does it will not be for some years -- so a sell off of the share had been somewhat premature.
